review.body_prefix: Thanks for the comprehensive Shortcut Guide update and validation. The Settings/UI direction looks good, but the Windows-key activation path still has correctness gaps that can break the normal activation shortcut and leave hold state or timers stale. Please address the two items below before merge.

proposed_comments.title: Separate Windows-key holds from the configured shortcut
proposed_comments.body:
### Separate Windows-key holds from the configured shortcut

**Severity:** `high`

The configured shortcut and the Windows-key hold callback both currently invoke `OnHotkeyEx` and signal the same event. Because the default shortcut itself contains Win, live key-state detection misclassifies it: `Off` can suppress the regular shortcut, while `TaskbarIndicators` can open only the indicator pane instead of the full guide. Route holds through a distinct source/event, keep the configured shortcut on the full-guide path, and make the release lifecycle handle both left and right Win keys, a release that occurs before the UI hook is installed, and only overlays actually opened by a hold. When refreshing the hold registration, clear and cancel only this module's pressed-key timers rather than deleting its normal centralized hotkeys, and skip the timers entirely when the action is `Off`.

proposed_comments.title: Persist normalized hold settings and validate before conversion
proposed_comments.body:
### Persist normalized hold settings and validate before conversion

**Severity:** `medium`

The ViewModel clamps both `win_key_action` and `press_time`, but its normalization notification only tracks the action value. A duration-only correction is therefore changed in memory without being saved or sent to Runner, so the invalid value is loaded again. Track both corrections, persist/send the normalized settings once, and extend the existing test to assert both serialized values. In the module interface, clamp the raw numeric duration before converting it to `UINT` and accept only the exact integral action values so negative, fractional, or corrupted JSON cannot select an unintended mode or delay.
